scope: Complete flat64 i_bs_create_bin instruction through native words and one generated C dispatcher. Owned sizing/allocation/error boundaries delegate to the existing full-kind native transplants. Not general binary matching, exception unwinding, Elixir or stateful-Isolate acceptance.
adaptations: project_dispatch extracts and hashes the whole generated case, then uses counted dependency substitutions. The entire sizing/allocation phases delegate to reviewed binary_size and writable/binary_begin helpers, including every native kind, normal/private/fresh path and ordered sizing error. No branch is a missing-helper optimization omission. The complete generated writer switch and error/relative-guard branches remain; flat64 is the existing mandatory representation profile.

Sizing precedes all allocation and respects later guest sizing failures even after the infrastructure ceiling was crossed. Atom badarg/system_limit classifications explicitly become bare native reason codes before atomic extended-info preparation. Float failures preserve native type/no_float/invalid distinctions and report the width term for invalid widths. Borrowed error values are rooted by the factory. The writer and temporary result expire before error allocation; abandoned backing can be swept immediately.

All operands are reloaded from real X/Y slots after allocating helpers. Physically dead X registers are cleared after sizing using the verified Live bound. Private append requires the producer/consumption proof and the existing dynamic alias guard; NOT_UNIQUE and other ownership refusals never become guest badarg. The source slot is consumed before later operands and final destination publication. The destination is resolved again after collection and assigned only on exact writer completion; successful Alloc heap credit is retained for following constructors.

Work charges bounded descriptor passes, dead-X clearing, intended writer bytes, actual initialized/copied storage bytes, conservative bignum-limb/private-alias scans, and actual successful collection cost. Storage helpers report byte work without independently charging reductions. Success and guard exits can yield only at their next real PC with valid roots, never replaying partially completed construction. One bounded 64 MiB operation, callbacks and full collection can overrun a slice; no hard-latency guarantee is claimed.

Host ceilings, OOM, ownership refusal and floating-environment failure have separate process/task/world outcomes. Public messages distinguish runtime resource limits, transport limits, execution outside admitted ownership profile and floating-point environment failure. Guest errors alone publish native reason/extended payload and use existing terminal expansion or their actual guard label. Stacktrace capture, catch/unwind and action-flag processing remain incomplete; pending native flags are not claimed as completed actions.

Fresh compiler-produced Erlang and standard OTP assembly execute integer dynamic/fixed and literal-big sources, float dynamic/fixed, binary dynamic/fixed/all, strings, UTF8/16/32, normal/private/frozen append, same-byte prefix sharing, Y destinations, extra heap credit and real guard failures. Core tests include allocation failures, partial-write error-payload OOM, immediate abandoned-backing sweep, post-publication budget yields, explicit ownership/size refusal and physical retirement. Public worker tests exercise nonempty copied results, peer progress/stop, replacement, guest errors and distinct runtime/transport limits.

683 normal result vectors compare to installed stock OTP. The pinned interpreter's invalid UTF8 followed by negative integer size still reports segment 2/integer/size; installed ARM JIT may report segment 1/utf8/type. Both actual executions are retained explicitly rather than normalized into a conformance claim. Comprehension matching and interprocedural private-entry facts remain excluded; the broader old binary_create_slice is still rejected independently for matching.
